title: Homebuyers treated as financial creditors - a landmark legal shift
p1:
What happens when a builder takes your hard-earned money but never delivers your dream home?

For years, many homebuyers felt powerless when real estate projects stalled or developers went bankrupt. But a landmark legal change gave them a stronger voice.
p2:
The surprising part? Homebuyers are not merely customers waiting for possession anymore. Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), they are recognised as financial creditors.

This recognition followed a major 2018 amendment, which brought amounts raised from homebuyers within the definition of financial debt.
p3:
What does this actually mean?

When a real estate developer enters insolvency proceedings, eligible homebuyers can participate in the process through their authorised representative in the Committee of Creditors. This gives them a say in decisions that may affect the project's future.

The practical takeaway: Your rights as a homebuyer do not necessarily disappear when a builder faces insolvency. Keep your allotment letter, payment receipts, agreement and correspondence safely documented. These records can matter when asserting your claim.
conclusion: Do you think recognising homebuyers as financial creditors has genuinely changed the balance of power between builders and buyers? Share your perspective.
